outcome: unfavorable respiratory outcomes at 40 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA)
severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia and death or mechanical ventilation at 40 weeks PMA
cohort: The study included 717 extremely preterm infants born at less than 29 weeks of gestation who received continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring.
finding: Physiologic data, particularly intermittent hypoxemia, independently predicted unfavorable respiratory outcomes and severe bronchopulmonary dysplasia/death/mechanical ventilation at 40 weeks PMA in extremely preterm infants, with predictive accuracy improving with advancing age.
